comments.author: lIl-IIIl
comments.story: More than half of YC startups don't have a dot com
comments.why: Randall explains origin of the xkcd name
comments.text: Randall wanted a unique short string associated with all his work. That way he could Google "xkcd" and find everything he ever did online. I believe he had a script that generated all possible 4-letter combinations and filtered out ones with any search results, and settled on "xkcd". But he became a victim of his own success when the comic became so popular and "xkcd" is now synonymous with the comic. Source: talk by Randall, might be this one but I'm not sure: [VIDEO] .

comments.author: pjmorris
comments.why: Knuth asking Munroe questions during Q&A
comments.text: There are many more important things about Knuth and his work, but one of my favorite stories about him is that he showed up at Randall Munroe's Google tech talk [0], and, during Q&A, asked Munroe "Have you thought about animated cartoons?" and "What is your n log n algorithm for searching?" I have a special respect for people who are both brilliant and humble, and Knuth is my poster person for that. [0] [VIDEO]

comments.author: tomhoward
comments.why: Knuth and Munroe exchange about Jobs story
comments.text: This story is the subject of a fascinating exchange between Knuth and Randall Munroe in Munroe's Authors@Google talk: [VIDEO] Knuth neither confirms nor outright denies the story, but says "I've only met [Jobs] a couple of times and in each case I was impressed by him probably more than he was impressed by me".

comments.author: antiform
comments.story: When Steve Jobs met Don Knuth
comments.why: Knuth comments on the Jobs anecdote
comments.text: Maybe Knuth was more of a rebel back in the day, but somehow I can't imagine him having that sort of response. In Randall Munroe's Authors@Google talk [ [VIDEO] ], Don Knuth asks him a question at ~21:30 and at ~25:30 Randall asks Knuth about this very anecdote. Knuth's response is "I've been told this story a number of times...but I was impressed by him more than he was impressed by me."
